business_problem: Traditional manual ground observations and aerial surveys made it challenging to collect accurate seal population data, particularly in hard-to-reach areas.
solution_summary: Natural England's two-year pilot used drones equipped with high-resolution cameras to capture seal imagery from 110 meters above the beach, helping survey hard-to-reach areas while minimising disturbance. Instance-segmentation AI processed the drone imagery to detect individual seals and distinguish adults from whitecoat pups, including when animals were grouped closely together. The detections supported a population count along an 8 kilometre stretch of shoreline and comparison with volunteer ground counts. The source does not name a drone, camera, AI model, or software product, and does not describe data storage, a downstream serving platform, or system integrations. Natural England says the approach could contribute to a comprehensive national picture of seal populations and help assess population changes and human impacts.

source_references.title: Using AI and drone technology to protect seals in Norfolk

evidence_quotes: The two-year project has used drone technology combined with Artificial Intelligence (AI) to monitor seal populations and their pups off the coast of Norfolk.

Instance segmentation (a type of AI), was then used to automatically detect individual seals from the drone imagery and distinguish between adult seals and whitecoat pups, even when grouped closely together.
The survey identified over 8,500 seals along an 8 kilometre stretch of shoreline, in comparison to a volunteer-led ground count which recorded more than 6,200 seals.
This project has shown that drones and the use of AI technology can be a cost and time efficient alternative method of monitoring seal populations.
